projects.title: Portfolio Website
projects.description: Built from scratch — responsive, animated, designed entirely by me.

sections.label: Overview
sections.content: This portfolio was designed and built entirely from scratch — no templates, no frameworks. The goal was to create something that felt genuinely mine: playful but professional, animated but readable, and technically solid under the hood.

sections.label: The Challenge
sections.content: Most portfolio templates feel generic. I wanted the site to reflect my dual background in design and development — meaning the code itself needed to be as considered as the visuals. That meant building each component intentionally: no Bootstrap grid, no copy-paste CSS.

sections.label: Key Implementation
sections.content: The skills marquee uses a duplicated list and a CSS @keyframes animation so it loops infinitely without JavaScript. Edge fades are handled entirely with mask-image. The modal system on the Wall page is vanilla JS — no libraries.

code.label: style.css — marquee animation

sections.label: What I Learned
sections.content: Working without a framework forced me to deeply understand CSS layout fundamentals — especially how stacking contexts, position: sticky, and clamp() interact. I also hit cross-browser issues with backdrop-filter that taught me to test on Safari early.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.content: A fully responsive, accessible portfolio site with custom animations, zero dependencies, and a clear design system — built and shipped for my 2026 job search.

projects.title: Data Analysis Project
projects.description: Exploratory data analysis and visualization for a class research project.

sections.label: Overview
sections.content: A class project exploring a real-world dataset using Python. The goal was to move from raw CSV data to clear, communicable findings through cleaning, analysis, and visualization.

sections.label: Approach
sections.content: Used Pandas for data cleaning and aggregation, then Matplotlib for charting. Prioritised readability over complexity — the audience was classmates, not data scientists.

code.label: analysis.py
code.body:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df.dropna(inplace=True)

summary = df.groupby('category')['value'].mean()
summary.plot(kind='bar', color='#8d79ff')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=150)

sections.label: Outcome
sections.content: A clean analysis with three data visualizations and a written interpretation. Submitted as part of a research methods course.

projects.title: Resource Central — UX Report
projects.description: Full UX research write-up: user testing, wireframes, and findings.

sections.label: Overview
sections.content: A full UX research write-up documenting the end-to-end design process for Resource Central — from initial user interviews through to final prototype and usability test results.

sections.label: Contents
sections.content: The report covers: research methodology, interview transcripts and affinity mapping, information architecture decisions, wireframe progression (low to high fidelity), usability test protocol and findings, and final design rationale.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.content: A 24-page documented research process that can stand alone as a portfolio artifact or be shared with employers as evidence of UX process thinking.

projects.title: Java Class Project
projects.description: Object-oriented application built for an intro to programming course.

sections.label: Overview
sections.content: An object-oriented Java application built for an intro to programming course. The project modelled a simple inventory system using core OOP principles: encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.

sections.label: Structure
sections.content: The application used a three-layer class hierarchy with a base Item class, extended by PhysicalItem and DigitalItem, each overriding a shared display() method.

code.label: Item.java

sections.label: Outcome
sections.content: A working inventory management CLI application demonstrating foundational OOP concepts. Submitted with full Javadoc documentation.
